harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with mode 1777 (rwxrwxrwt) owned by root:root, so any user can create files but only the owner (or root) can delete/rename their own files. Verified the sticky-bit behavior with two test users before and after a full node restart, which also confirmed persistence.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop, set ownership root:root and mode 1777 on node1
Verified with two temporary users (dropuser1, dropuser2) that both can create files but neither can delete the other's file (only the owner/root can)
Cleaned up test users and test files
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state of /srv/drop
Issued a non-interactive `systemctl reboot` on node1 with the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until it became reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (21de1f79-... -> 64614bbd-...), proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop mode/ownership and sticky-bit delete-denial behavior post-restart with fresh test users, then cleaned up

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as shared writable directory with sticky bit preventing cross-user deletion
evidence.summary: Directory created, chowned root:root, chmod 1777; ls -ld shows drwxrwxrwt; two different users could each create a file but dropuser2's attempt to rm dropuser1's file was denied with 'Operation not permitted', while dropuser1 could delete its own file

evidence.requirement: Environment left clean of test artifacts before restart
evidence.summary: Removed temporary dropuser1/dropuser2 accounts; /srv/drop remains 1777 root:root

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 21de1f79-e793-4c36-923a-f4af0bbea55e, uptime since 2026-09-29 08:15:55, and confirmed /srv/drop mode/ownership (drwxrwxrwt root:root) prior to restart
Issued backgrounded `sudo -n systemctl reboot`; command returned 'reboot acknowledged and issued' before the node dropped
Two consecutive poll attempts failed with connection timeout/reset, showing the node was mid-restart

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 64614bbd-b64f-4beb-8957-1785db4da769, differing from the pre-restart 21de1f79-e793-4c36-923a-f4af0bbea55e, with fresh uptime 2026-09-29 08:16:25

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the required directory and its behavior
evidence.summary: /srv/drop retained mode drwxrwxrwt owner root:root after reboot; re-ran the two-user create/delete test and confirmed cross-user delete was again denied ('Operation not permitted') while same-owner delete succeeded; test artifacts cleaned up, leaving /srv/drop empty and correctly configured

attempts.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with mode 1777 (rwxrwxrwt) owned by root:root, so any user can create files but only the owner (or root) can delete/rename their own files. Verified the sticky-bit behavior with two test users before and after a full node restart, which also confirmed persistence.
